svg.title: A 22-year-old man is under general anesthesia with a volatile agent and succinylcholine for shoulder repair. Twenty-five minutes in, his end-tidal carbon dioxide keeps climbing despite increased ventilation. HR 148. There is masseter rigidity, generalized muscle rigidity, and mottled skin. His core temperature has just begun to rise.
svg.desc: Rising end-tidal carbon dioxide with tachycardia and muscle rigidity during a volatile agent and succinylcholine is malignant hyperthermia; hypercarbia and tachycardia come first and the temperature rise is a later sign. Stopping the trigger and giving dantrolene are the two actions that change the outcome. Thyroid storm also brings fever and tachycardia, but it does not cause masseter rigidity minutes after induction. Cooling and increased minute ventilation are added, not warming and a slower rate.
